title: Deterministic vs Probabilistic: UCB and Thompson Sampling in Machine Learning

cues.en: -: Hello, and welcome back to the course on machine learning.
cues.zh: 講師：大家好，歡迎回到機器學習課程。

cues.en: I hope you enjoyed the previous tutorials and now you're quite confident with the upper confidence bound and the Thompson sampling algorithm, or at least the intuition behind them,
cues.zh: 希望你喜歡前幾堂，現在對 UCB 與 Thompson 抽樣，至少背後概念，已經相當有把握。

cues.en: and today we're going to quickly compare the two because they do solve the same problem.
cues.zh: 今天快速比較兩者，因為解的是相同問題。

cues.en: They solve the problem of the multi-armed bandit, and let's have a look at some of the pros and cons of each of the algorithms.
cues.zh: 都是多臂吃角子老虎，看看各自優缺點。

cues.en: So of course there's lots and lots of different advantages and disadvantages and differences between the two, but we'll just highlight the main ones.
cues.zh: 當然有很多優缺點和差異，只突出主要幾項。

cues.en: So here we've got the two algorithms.
cues.zh: 這是兩個演算法。

cues.en: On the left we've got the UCB and the image from the intuition tutorial that will help us kinda remember what it's about and the Thompson sampling algorithm and the same,
cues.zh: 左邊 UCB，加上概念課圖片，幫助回想；Thompson 抽樣也一樣，

cues.en: the image behind it.
cues.zh: 放了背後概念的圖。

cues.en: So the first characteristic is probably, that is different, is that the UCB is a deterministic algorithm, and actually, there's lots of different,
cues.zh: 第一個不同特性，UCB 是確定式演算法，其實還有很多不同，

cues.en: there's lots of different modifications to the UCB algorithm.
cues.zh: 不同的修改版本。

cues.en: You can find them online.
cues.zh: 網路可以找到。

cues.en: There's lots of different white papers on how the UCB algorithm can be modified to improve it and to make it better at one thing,
cues.zh: 很多論文討論怎麼修改 UCB，改善某項能力，

cues.en: or adds one advantage, maybe makes it a bit better result, but it makes it more computationally intensive, or the other way around, and so on.
cues.zh: 或增加一項優勢，結果也許更好，但計算量更大，或反過來，等等。

cues.en: But all of that, all of those algorithms belong to a family of UCB algorithms, or upper confident bound algorithms, which are all deterministic, and basically what that means is
cues.zh: 但這些都屬於 UCB、信賴上界演算法家族，都是確定式，基本意思

cues.en: that it is very straightforward.
cues.zh: 就是非常明確直接。

cues.en: So once you have a certain round,
cues.zh: 在某個特定回合，

cues.en: if it's very straightforward, what's going to happen?
cues.zh: 會發生什麼，非常明確。

cues.en: Or you just look at the upper confidence bound, and whichever one has the highest, that's the one you pick.
cues.zh: 看信賴上界，哪個最高就選哪個。

cues.en: You pull the algorithm, the yes, you pull the lever, yes, then you do get like a random value from the machine.
cues.zh: 執行演算法，對，拉把手，確實從機器得到隨機值。

cues.en: But that's on the side of the machine.
cues.zh: 但那是機器端的事。

cues.en: So that randomness is on the machine, but then, whatever value you get, it is very determined, it is very deterministic,
cues.zh: 隨機性來自機器；取得任意值之後，UCB 如何處理它，

cues.en: what the UCB is going to do with that value.
cues.zh: 是完全確定的。

cues.en: And so all the steps that the UCB actually takes, they are very deterministic.
cues.zh: UCB 所採取的每個步驟，都很確定。

cues.en: There's no randomness in the algorithm, itself.
cues.zh: 演算法本身沒有隨機性。

cues.en: Whereas, on the other hand, the Thompson sampling algorithm is a probabilistic algorithm because in the algorithm itself, it has these distributions which represent
cues.zh: 相對地，Thompson 抽樣是機率式，因為演算法本身有這些分布，代表

cues.en: our perception of the world and where we think the actual expected returns of each of those machines might lie,
cues.zh: 對世界的認知，以及認為各機器真正期望報酬可能位於哪裡。

cues.en: and therefore every time we are implementing or iterating in the Thompson sampling algorithm,
cues.zh: 因此每次執行或迭代 Thompson 抽樣，

cues.en: we actually generate random values from those distributions.
cues.zh: 都從這些分布產生隨機值。

cues.en: So if you rerun a round in the UCB algorithm, just one given round, after you've received the previous value from the machine,
cues.zh: 如果 UCB 某回合，在收到機器先前的值後，

cues.en: and then you rerun the round, it's always going to be the same result, whereas in the Thompson sampling algorithm, after you've received the previous value from the machine and you rerun the current round,
cues.zh: 重新跑這回合，結果總相同；Thompson 抽樣收到先前值後，重新跑目前回合，

cues.en: it's always going to different because you're always sampling from your distributions which characterize your perception of the world,
cues.zh: 結果會不同，因為一直從代表世界認知的分布抽樣。

cues.en: and that is a whole different type of algorithm.
cues.zh: 這是完全不同類型。

cues.en: It's a probabilistic algorithm.
cues.zh: 是機率式演算法。

cues.en: And those two things, they actually have a few different implications.
cues.zh: 這兩點會帶來一些不同影響。

cues.en: So for instance, one important one is that the UCB requires an update at every round.
cues.zh: 例如重要的一點，UCB 每回合都需要更新。

cues.en: So basically the value that you get back from the machine, so once you've pulled the lever and you get a value back from that machine, that value, you have to incorporate it right away
cues.zh: 拉把手、收到機器傳回值後，必須立刻納入，

cues.en: in order to proceed to the next round.
cues.zh: 才能進下一回合。

cues.en: You cannot proceed to the next round until you have incorporated that value, until you have made an adjustment to the algorithm based on that value,
cues.zh: 沒納入、沒根據這值調整演算法，就不能繼續，

cues.en: because if you don't make the adjustment, then nothing changes and you're going to be stuck.
cues.zh: 因為不調整，就什麼都沒變，會卡住。

cues.en: Whereas in the Thompson sampling, it can accommodate delayed feedback, and this is very important.
cues.zh: 但 Thompson 抽樣能容納延遲回饋，這很重要。

cues.en: This basically means that, if you pull the lever and you only will get the result or you will only know the result of pulling the lever 500 rounds
cues.zh: 意思是，拉把手後，要過五百回合

cues.en: down the track, not right away, you'll only get to know the result 500 rounds later, the Thompson sampling algorithm will still work.
cues.zh: 才知道結果，不是立刻知道，而是五百回合後，Thompson 抽樣仍能運作。

cues.en: Why will it still work?
cues.zh: 為什麼？

cues.en: Because if you now run the algorithm without even updating your perception of the world, you're still going to get a new set
cues.zh: 因為不更新世界認知，再跑演算法，仍會得到一組新的

cues.en: of hypothetical bandits.
cues.zh: 假想機器。

cues.en: You're going to generate a new expected return for every bandit because you are generating them in a probabilistic manner.
cues.zh: 會為每台產生新期望報酬，因為採機率方式產生。

cues.en: And this is very important to understand, because this gives the Thompson sampling that advantage that you don't have to update the algorithm with the result every time.
cues.zh: 這點很重要，讓 Thompson 抽樣有優勢，不必每次都用結果更新。

cues.en: And in terms of bandits, of course that doesn't really matter that much, because if you're playing in the casino and if some hypothetical person is playing
cues.zh: 對拉霸機當然不太重要，因為假想有人在賭場玩，

cues.en: in the casino and they're pulling these levers, they get to see the results right away, so they could update the algorithm.
cues.zh: 拉把手立刻就看到結果，可以更新。

cues.en: But in terms of websites and ads, that is a big deal.
cues.zh: 但網站與廣告就很重要。

cues.en: So not even just displaying ads on a website, or you could use this for AB testing different,
cues.zh: 不只在網站放廣告，也能用於測試不同，

cues.en: instead of AB testing the different layouts of your website, you could use a Thompson sampling algorithm
cues.zh: 與其對網站不同版面做 A/B 測試，可以用 Thompson 抽樣，

cues.en: to have that balance between exploitation, exploration, right away.
cues.zh: 立即平衡探索與利用。

cues.en: So basically anything you're doing on the web with Thompson sampling or solving a multi-armed bandit problem for your business or for a business on the web,
cues.zh: 基本上，無論在網路用 Thompson 抽樣，或為業務、網路業務解多臂吃角子老虎問題，

cues.en: you're getting all these thousands and tens of thousands of clicks, and to update the algorithm right away, that would be very highly computationally costly,
cues.zh: 會得到成千上萬點擊，立刻更新演算法的計算成本非常高，

cues.en: or it might require additional resources and a complex process.
cues.zh: 或需要額外資源與複雜流程。

cues.en: Whereas what the Thompson sampling algorithm allows you to do is to update your dataset or your information in the algorithm in a batch manner.
cues.zh: Thompson 抽樣則允許以批次方式更新資料或演算法資訊。

cues.en: So you wait until you get 500 clicks or you wait until you get 5,000 clicks, you update the algorithm.
cues.zh: 等五百次或五千次點擊，再更新。

cues.en: Then you let it run, and then it runs, runs, runs, and then you get another 5,000 clicks and then you update the algorithm again, and it will still work,
cues.zh: 繼續跑，再跑，等另外五千次點擊後再次更新，仍然能運作。

cues.en: and that's a very important thing, that flexibility that the Thompson sampling algorithm creates.
cues.zh: 這種彈性是 Thompson 抽樣非常重要的特點。

cues.en: And finally, again, we're not gonna go into too much detail on the pros and cons, but the Thompson sampling algorithm is actually,
cues.zh: 最後，不會深入所有優缺點，但 Thompson 抽樣其實

cues.en: it has better empirical evidence than the UCB, and you'll find this phrase, better empirical evidence, and that's because, up until recently,
cues.zh: 比 UCB 有更好的實證支持。你會看到「更好的實證支持」這句話，因為直到不久前，

cues.en: the theory behind the Thompson sampling algorithm, or the whole research, wasn't complete.
cues.zh: 它背後的理論或整體研究都還不完整。

cues.en: It's only been researched in a lot of detail just a few years ago, and now you can find a lot of information on Thompson sampling algorithm.
cues.zh: 幾年前才深入研究，現在能找到很多相關資訊。

cues.en: But previously people just see that, from experimental evidence, that Thompson sampling algorithm does work better than the UCB, and that's exactly what we're going to see.
cues.zh: 但先前大家只是從實驗證據看到，Thompson 抽樣確實比 UCB 好，接著也會看到。

cues.en: Spoiler alert, that's exactly what you're going to see in the practical tutorials for this section.
cues.zh: 先劇透，這個單元的實作正會看到這件事。

cues.en: So we're going to be now coding the, or Head Lund will walk you through coding the same exercise, the same problem that we had previously with the UCB.
cues.zh: 現在要寫程式，或者說 Hadelin 帶你寫，解和 UCB 先前相同的練習與問題。

cues.en: Now we're going to be, or you're going to be solving it with the Thompson sampling algorithm and you will see, actually, some very interesting results.
cues.zh: 這次用 Thompson 抽樣，會看到很有意思的結果。

cues.en: We'll leave it at that, and I hope you enjoyed these intuition tutorials, and off we go to the practical side of things.
cues.zh: 先到這裡，希望你喜歡這些概念課，接著進實作。

cues.en: Can't wait for you to get started.
cues.zh: 期待你開始。

cues.en: Head Lund will show you all around, and I'll see you back here next time.
cues.zh: Hadelin 會帶你操作，下次在這裡見。

cues.en: Until then, enjoy machine learning.
cues.zh: 在那之前，祝你享受機器學習的樂趣。
